newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: IMF grants Argentina 3rd $154 mln standby loan.
newsitem.headline: IMF grants Argentina 3rd $154 mln standby loan.

text.p: The Argentine Economy Ministry said Monday that the International Monetary Fund had authorized a third standby loan disimbursement of 107 million Special Drawing Rights, equivalent to about $154 million.
The ministry said in a statement that this installment would take the country's total debt obligations with the IMF to $6.38 billion.

The Argentine government said the latest IMF loan tranche was granted following the approval of the country's fiscal goals for the month of September by an IMF mission currently visiting Buenos Aires.

"This shows the Fund's continued support for the Argentine economic program, based on maintaining macroeconomic stability and extending structural reforms designed to consolidate sustained growth and the benefits of integrating Argentina into global markets," said the ministry statement.

In October the IMF's board approved changes to Argentina's economic targets originally as a condition for the $1.2 billion standby agreement, after the country requested a waiver on its $2.5 billion budget deficit goal.
Argentina then postponed talks on a longer-term Extended Fund Facility to early next year.
